Feast-day recipes

Pan de Muerto

Served at: Dia de los Angelitos · Dia de los Muertos

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 35 min

Pan de Muerto is a traditional Mexican sweet bread baked especially for Día de los Muertos and Día de los Angelitos, celebrations honoring deceased loved ones and children who have passed. This bread is often decorated with bone-shaped dough pieces and flavored with orange blossom water or anise, symbolizing the cycle of life and death.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups all-purpose flour (480 g)
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar (100 g)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup whole milk, warm (120 ml)
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened (115 g)
  • 4 large eggs
  • 1 tablespoon orange zest
  • 1 teaspoon orange blossom water (optional)
  • 1 teaspoon anise seeds (optional)
  • 1/4 cup warm water (60 ml)
  • Extra flour for dusting
  • 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted (60 g)
  • Granulated sugar for sprinkling

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, salt, and anise seeds (if using).
  3. In another bowl, whisk together warm milk, softened butter, eggs, orange zest, and orange blossom water (if using).
  4. Add the yeast mixture and the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix until a dough forms.
  5. Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  6. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1.5 to 2 hours or until doubled in size.
  7. Punch down the dough and divide a small portion to create the bone decorations later.
  8. Shape the main dough into a round loaf and place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
  9. Roll the reserved dough into thin strips and shape them into bone-like decorations; place them on top of the loaf.
  10. Cover the loaf and let it rise again for 30-45 minutes until puffed.
  11. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  12. Bake the bread for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped.
  13. Remove from oven and immediately brush the entire loaf with melted butter.
  14. Sprinkle granulated sugar generously over the buttered bread and let it cool completely before serving.

Tips

  • For a more authentic flavor, use fresh orange zest and orange blossom water if available.
  • You can add a few drops of anise extract if you don't have anise seeds.
  • If you prefer, shape smaller individual loaves instead of one large loaf for easier serving.
